claims: shutil copy functions do not preserve all metadata.
copy2 attempts metadata, may preserve only what is available, and does not raise solely because metadata cannot be copied.
The platform-specific known loss examples and Linux extended-attribute qualification are scoped to the pinned docs.
claim_mappings.governing_scope: CPython pinned documentation; not an assertion of complete per-file metadata reporting.
claim_mappings.unresolved_uncertainty: Destination filesystem and individual metadata support vary; application-level metadata inventory is future work.

claim_mappings.final_section: Copy and metadata path; Alternatives and decisions retained
claims: copyfileobj defaults to chunked copying to avoid uncontrolled memory use.
CPython functions may use fast-copy paths; Linux documentation names sendfile and Windows documentation names a larger buffer/memoryview path; the docs describe fallback conditions.
claim_mappings.governing_scope: Pinned CPython docs and implementation; does not assert universal speed, progress callback support, or measured performance.
claim_mappings.unresolved_uncertainty: Performance and cancellation latency require application benchmarks on Linux and Windows.

claims: shutil.move uses rename on the same filesystem and copy-then-remove across filesystems.
os.rename has different overwrite behavior on Windows and Unix in the pinned Python docs.
os.replace overwrites an existing file when permitted and documents atomic rename as a POSIX requirement.
Linux renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE refuses an existing target where supported.
claim_mappings.governing_scope: The Linux primitive is Linux-specific and filesystem-dependent. Python os.replace atomicity is documented as a POSIX requirement. Windows and each destination filesystem require tests.
claim_mappings.unresolved_uncertainty: No behavior tests were run; exact replacement-target compare-and-swap is not guaranteed by a path recheck followed by replace.

claims: For buffered Python file objects, flush before os.fsync.
Pinned docs state Unix fsync and Windows _commit behavior.
The proposal does not infer crash durability of a renamed directory entry from file fsync or atomic visibility.
claim_mappings.governing_scope: Sync calls and rename semantics as documented by CPython; the proposal distinguishes these from a universal hardware persistence guarantee.
claim_mappings.unresolved_uncertainty: Filesystem, device, controller, Windows directory-entry, and network persistence behavior is untested.

claim_mappings.final_section: Validation plan; Criticism dispositions F1 and F4
claims: The pinned copy2 test verifies selected mode/time/flag behavior.
The pinned other-filesystem move tests mock rename and delegate to common move tests; they are not real-mount durability tests.
claim_mappings.governing_scope: Source-level test setup and assertions only.
claim_mappings.unresolved_uncertainty: Tests were inspected, not executed; application and platform matrix remains future work.

design_inferences_and_limits.claim: Destination-local exclusive staging plus same-filesystem publication avoids exposing the final name to partial-copy writes.
design_inferences_and_limits.basis: Implementation design derived from the publication semantics above; it is a proposal and has not been executed.

design_inferences_and_limits.claim: An initial identity check followed by path-based os.replace retains a residual race against uncoordinated external writers.
design_inferences_and_limits.basis: Inference from path-based replace semantics; portable Python docs do not offer a compare-and-swap replacement conditioned on the prior file identity.

design_inferences_and_limits.claim: Modification-time capture before the read defines which useful timestamp the application promises.
design_inferences_and_limits.basis: Product policy recommendation; application behavior and filesystem precision require validation.
